blocks: Played live at a synth meetup on November 14, 2026, in Ableton/Live at 60 BPM in 4/4 with the Novation/Launchpad/Pro/Mk3 and the Microfreak. Four tracks carry the performance, colored after the Launchpad's sequencer tracks: orange and green for the MicroFreak, purple and coral for the drums.

The recording was rendered after the meetup from a copy of the Set. The MicroFreak comes from archive tracks that recorded the live tracks after their faders, so the live fader moves are in it. The drums play back from the recorded MIDI, 4 dB louder than they were in the room. Reverb was added to the archive tracks, and three seconds were cut from the green track at 02:42. The MP3 is loudness-normalized to −16 LUFS. There is no spoken commentary.
GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set — the tracks, routing, mixer moves and drum pads of the Ableton Live Set.

Microfreak/Preset/259 Infini Pad — the whole performance, played from the MicroFreak's keys. A paraphonic pad on the BASS oscillator with a slow attack; key pressure adds Fold and Saturate and opens the filter.

192 kbps stereo MP3 at 44.1 kHz, 4:40, made from the 24-bit, 48 kHz WAV exported from Ableton Live 11.3.43 on November 14, 2026 (26.11.14-Fallveter-04-perf-post.wav). Integrated loudness −16.0 LUFS; true peak −2.2 dBFS; loudness range 14.9 LU.

The WAV was raised 16.8 dB and passed through a true-peak limiter at −2 dBFS, run at 192 kHz. The limiter takes 4 to 6 dB off the hand-struck cue balls between 04:09 and 04:18 and up to 2 dB off a few drum strikes between 01:04 and 02:11; the rest passes unchanged.
Type 1 standard MIDI file at 60 BPM in 4/4, 4:40 long, aligned with the episode recording; one beat is one second. The tempo track carries a marker for each chapter.

"Piano Pool" holds the 116 strikes Launchpad sequencer track 2 played on the Piano Pool drum rack, on MIDI channel 2. "Cueball Drums" holds the 16 strikes played by hand on Launchpad track 4, on channel 4. Notes use Live's pad numbers: C1 (MIDI note 36) to D♯2 (51) for Piano Pool. GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set/Track/POOL PIANO DRUMS- LPP sequencer track 2 lists the sample on each pad.
The Set stored most sequencer strikes twice at the same moment; the file keeps one of each. The MicroFreak was played from its own keys, and that playing left no MIDI.

The Session View mixer of the copy saved after the performance, with the transport stopped at bar 71. MF AUDIO 1, POOL PIANO DRUMS, MF AUDIO 2 and Cueball Drums run left to right, followed by the folded END, rec archive and utility groups; the two return tracks and the Main track sit off the right edge.

Live saved the Set during the performance as 26.11.14-Fallveter-04-perf-pre.als. It kept recording for about an hour; the performance is the first 4:40, between the locators "1" and "end". At 60 BPM a beat lasts one second, so beat numbers in the Arrangement read as seconds of the episode. Ableton/Live/UG/07 Session View/05 Recording Sessions into the Arrangement

This page describes the copy saved afterwards, 26.11.14-Fallveter-04-perf-post.als, which rendered the episode. In it, MF AUDIO 1 and MF AUDIO 2 are switched off and the rec archive tracks play to Master, so the MicroFreak comes from the archive recordings. The drums were raised by 4 dB, reverb sends were added to the archive tracks, and the Arrangement ends at 4:40.

The Microfreak arrives on external inputs 1/2 at both MF AUDIO 1 (orange) and MF AUDIO 2 (green). Both are armed with monitoring on Auto, so each records takes from the MicroFreak and loops them in Session View. Ableton/Live/UG/17 Routing and IO/01 Monitoring
Rec MF AUDIO 1 and rec MF AUDIO 2 record the two MicroFreak tracks after their faders. Ableton/Live/UG/17 Routing and IO/05 Internal Routings

POOL PIANO DRUMS (purple) listens to channel 2 of the Launchpad Pro's MIDI port, where Launchpad sequencer track 2 plays the Piano Pool drum rack. Cueball Drums (coral) listens to channel 4. Launchpad/UG/09 Sequencer/13 Settings/05 MIDI Channel
LPP to MF passes the Launchpad's channel 1 to the MicroFreak but carried no notes during the performance. MF to LPP is not armed, so the MicroFreak's keys left no MIDI.
No track is assigned to either side of the crossfader. Ableton/Live/UG/18 Mixing/05 Using Live's Crossfader
A-Reverb holds a Reverb and B-Delay a Delay.
Sixteen unnamed scenes. "silence" clips sit in scenes 1, 8 and 9 on the four main tracks, in scene 16 on MF AUDIO 1 and MF AUDIO 2, and in scenes 1 to 9 on the END tracks.
The performance takes sit in scenes 2 to 4: "MF AUDIO 1 22", "MF AUDIO 1 24-1" and "MF AUDIO 1 27-1" on MF AUDIO 1, and "MF AUDIO 2 8" and "MF AUDIO 2 11-1" on MF AUDIO 2.

The coral track. It plays a drum rack of 38 pool-cue strikes, Pool Cue 12 on F1 up to Pool Cue 14 on G4, from Launchpad track 4 on MIDI channel 4.
Its only notes in the performance are sixteen strikes played by hand between 04:09 and 04:21: Pool Cue 28 on F♯4 and Pool Cue 45 on F4. Its pan moved to 34L at 00:42.

The orange MicroFreak track. It recorded three takes during the performance and looped each one: "MF AUDIO 1 22" from 00:20, "MF AUDIO 1 24-1" from 02:08 and "MF AUDIO 1 27-1" from 03:44.
Its fader moved live: down to −12 dB at 01:24, back near −5 dB at 01:34, out from 03:20 to 03:25, back at −6 dB at 03:31, and out again by 04:39. Its pan moved to 34R at 00:42.
In this copy of the Set the track is switched off, and GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set/Track/rec archive/Rec MF AUDIO 1 plays what it sent out.
The green MicroFreak track. It recorded two takes and looped each one: "MF AUDIO 2 8" from 01:00 to 02:44, and the four-second "MF AUDIO 2 11-1" from 03:04.
Its pan moved to 34R at 00:42, and its fader came down from 04:34 to 04:35.
In this copy of the Set the track is switched off, and GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set/Track/rec archive/rec MF AUDIO 2 plays what it sent out.

Recorded both MicroFreak tracks for the whole meetup, about an hour. During the performance its tracks sent only to the returns; in this copy they play to Master, and the episode's MicroFreak audio comes from them.

Records GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set/Track/MF AUDIO 1 after its fader, so the live fader moves are in the recording. Sends to GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set/Track/A-Reverb at −8.7 dB, added after the performance.
Records GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set/Track/MF AUDIO 2 after its fader. Sends to GitP/A/Session/26/11/14-Sat/Set/Track/A-Reverb at −6 dB.
After the performance its fader was lowered from −6 dB at 02:00 to −9 dB at 02:48, and three seconds were cut out at 02:42.
MIDI routing between the Launchpad Pro and the MicroFreak, and a network audio plugin.
Passes the Launchpad Pro's channel 1 to the MicroFreak. It carried no notes during the performance.
Passes the MicroFreak back to the Launchpad Pro. It was not armed, so nothing was recorded from the MicroFreak's keys.
A plugin on a track with no input that sends only to the returns.
A line of Qbit Brass goes into the Launchpad and comes back as a second voice. A tiny descant slips over it. Then the commentary mic goes quiet and the MicroFreak carries on.

Listen for the second voice at 00:33. It began as a pattern on track 2 of the Launchpad/Sequencer, then went into Live as audio. The commentary calls out live recording into the sequencer, panning and reverb as the layers take shape.
